title: Process Bounded Standard Input
concept: Treat input as data with resource limits

writing.summary: Treat input as data with resource limits.
writing.rule: Check byte limits before retaining input and validate complete records.
writing.explanation:
Standard input makes a tool composable: a file can feed the same parser as typed input. Rust strings are UTF-8; byte length and character count answer different questions. A memory budget is measured in bytes, so an emoji can consume several bytes of the budget. A record title is a nonblank line after trimming, with at most 80 Unicode scalar values in this lab.

Reject the complete input if its byte size exceeds the supplied budget or any title is too long. Ignore blank lines and keep record order. A production streaming parser additionally stops accumulation as it reads; this exercise receives an already bounded string to isolate validation. The companion reads through a limited reader and detects one byte beyond its limit. Do not advertise a post-read length check as protection against an unbounded stream.

The route project is Task Ledger: first keep a reproducible source history, then expose its data through a CLI and HTTP boundary, persist it in SQL, diagnose failures and prepare a release. This lesson owns one contract in that project. Run the worked example before changing the starter and explain which input makes the tempting shortcut fail.

Terminal practice: Create input.txt, then run cargo run -- import < input.txt; inspect stderr for an oversized record.

The compiler lab is independent of the reading question. Edit solution.rs; the app supplies a separate caller with normal, empty and adversarial inputs. A successful unchanged demonstration does not prove your implementation. After the lab, apply the same contract to the route companion project. Its README separates the on-device adapter from the desktop Cargo/TCP profile.
writing.exampleCaption: The worked implementation exercises treat input as data with resource limits. Its tests demonstrate the stated finite contract.
writing.task: Reject input exceeding max_bytes; trim lines, omit blanks, reject titles longer than 80 Unicode scalar values, and preserve order. Keep the public signature. Open the compiler lab and edit solution.rs; do not edit the private verification caller.
writing.success: The separate caller accepts the changed solution and rejects unchanged TODO, a wrong implementation and a printed success message.
writing.question: Which size controls a UTF-8 input memory budget?
answers: Only the number of visible characters
writing.feedback: An emoji can fit one scalar position while exceeding a three-byte budget.
